note:
FH.14b: a host-less client never pairs a catch-all route of another project. Three npm packages in one repo (packages/a, b, c, each with its own package.json, so each is a nested PROJECT and its ROUTE / ENDPOINT qnames carry ` @packages/

`). packages/a calls `fetch('/x')` and `fetch('/*')` with no host and no base, and serves `GET /x`; packages/b serves only an Express catch-all `app.get('/*', serveIndex)` (a dev server's SPA fallback, the shape of medusa's admin-bundler); packages/c calls `fetch('/*')` and serves its own catch-all. A catch-all stays literal in the path normaliser, so the only clients that reach it are ones whose own path is the catch-all (medusa's `subscribers.get("*")` read as an HTTP GET). Before FH.14b (debug CLI at 2e9ef8b7): `[http] routes=3 endpoints=3 paired=5`, a's `/*` paired b's and c's catch-alls and c's `/*` paired b's as well as its own. After it a catch-all of another project is out of a host-less client's ladder, so a's `/*` stays unpaired (an unpaired_endpoint row, never a guess) and c's pairs only its own project's catch-all. Recall alone cannot see the wrong pairs, so the precision gate is the forbid rows. Deliberately not bound to a matrix cell: typescript/http_client and typescript/http_server are scored elsewhere.

expect_nodes.name: endpoint:GET:/* @packages/a
expect_nodes.note: `fetch('/*')` in packages/a: no host, no base

expect_nodes.name: endpoint:GET:/* @packages/c
expect_nodes.note: `fetch('/*')` in packages/c: no host, no base

expect_nodes.name: GET /* @packages/b
expect_nodes.note: another package's catch-all, present so the forbid rows are not vacuous

expect_edges.note: a catch-all inside the client's own project still pairs

forbid.note: another project's catch-all beside the client's own (matched before FH.14b)
